gates.reason: Product identity is NOT substantiated. No Microsoft product named 'Visual Basic for Mac' was found in Microsoft KB product lists (S02-S05), and period Mac trade press describes its absence in 1996 (S17, weakly S18). Microsoft's Mac BASIC products were MS BASIC Interpreter 1.0-3.0 (1984-1986), BASIC Compiler 1.0, and QuickBASIC 1.00 for Apple Macintosh (1988, last update 1.00e 1992). The only Microsoft 'Visual Basic' shipped on Mac was VBA inside Office apps (Power Macintosh Office apps by Oct 1994, S28; Word 98 Macintosh Edition, S06; removed in Office 2008, S20; restored in Office 2011, S21/S23) and a planned 1996 VBScript for Mac (S19). The narration's claim is contradicted by the evidence gathered; the script change and the visual approach are producer/Writing Lead decisions.

No authenticated screenshot of a 'Visual Basic for Mac' can exist because no such product was identified. Adjacent screenshot candidates (IA mac_MSBASIC_1/2 emulator captures S07/S08; WinWorld S12/S13; Macintosh Repository S14) carry no creator credit or license record, and none were downloaded. MacWEEK page scans (S17-S19) have unknown rights. Nothing is cleared.

claims.text: Microsoft did release a product called "Visual Basic for Mac"
claims.note: Not an absence-of-search argument alone: Microsoft's own applicability lists enumerate Mac BASIC products without any Visual Basic, and MacWEEK (1996-02-05) states VB for the Mac was absent. A 1996 announcement of a Mac VBScript (S19) and VBA in Mac Office (S06) are different products.

Nearest Microsoft Mac BASIC: QuickBASIC 1.00 for Apple Macintosh, 1988, maintenance update 1.00e April 1992 (secondary date). VBA in Mac Office: in Power Macintosh Office apps including Excel 5.0 by Oct 1994 (Microsoft KB text, S28) and Word 98 Macintosh Edition (S06). That is a macro language inside Office, not a product called Visual Basic for Mac.
No product to evaluate. Secondary sources describe QuickBASIC for Mac as stagnant and not 32-bit clean; that is not the named product.

QuickBASIC for Mac: 1988 to last update 1992, discontinuation 1995 (secondary) - not quick. Mac VBA: ~1994/1998 to removal announced 2006, restored 2011. The quick-abandonment story best fits Apple's MacBASIC (cancelled 1985, never released, S15), which was not a Microsoft product.

claims.text: it existed and nobody liked it
claims.note: Existence of the named product is contradicted; reception is unverifiable.

claims.text: [VISUAL] screenshot of VB for Mac if one can be found; otherwise a "404 Not Found" joke graphic
claims.note: No authentic VB-for-Mac screenshot is possible. A 404 gag cannot serve as evidence and requires producer approval; it would also be misleading if the narration still claims the product existed.

candidate_referents.name: Microsoft QuickBASIC 1.00 for Apple Macintosh
candidate_referents.fit: Most plausible 'Microsoft BASIC for Mac that went nowhere'; not Visual Basic, not early 90s launch

candidate_referents.name: Apple MacBASIC
candidate_referents.fit: Matches 'abandoned quickly' but was Apple's and never shipped

candidate_referents.name: Visual Basic for Applications in Office for Mac
candidate_referents.dates: in Power Macintosh Office apps (Excel 5.0 era) by Oct 1994; Word 98 Macintosh Edition; removed Office 2008 (announced 2006-08); restored Office 2011
candidate_referents.fit: The only 'Visual Basic' Microsoft shipped on Mac; a macro language, not a standalone IDE. The mid-90s Excel 5 for Mac is the closest match to 'early-to-mid 90s, disliked'.

candidate_referents.name: Visual Basic Script (VBScript) for the Mac
candidate_referents.dates: announced for summer 1996 (MacWEEK 1996-06-03); actual ship not verified
candidate_referents.fit: VB-branded, Microsoft, Mac, mid-90s; web scripting, not an app builder

candidate_referents.name: REALbasic
candidate_referents.fit: Commonly described as VB-like for Mac; not Microsoft, not early 90s
